description: Lock-window-aware lock-vs-float-down recommendation for a deal already in the pipeline. Given a known lock-expiration date, the currently locked rate, and the float-down cost, returns a defensible hold-lock vs exercise-float-down call a loan officer can document — combining recent market movement (1w/2w/4w) with payment and break-even math on this loan. Builds on the same recent-movement signal as assess_buy_timing but framed around the lock window/expiration. Not a rate forecast.

float_down_bps.description: optional improvement in bps if float_down_rate omitted

name: assess_rate_lock

assumed_defaults.description: Inputs the caller did not supply that were filled in with defaults. State these explicitly to the user, since they drive the numbers.

closing_costs.description: Closing costs in dollars assumed because the caller did not supply them.

float_down_cost.description: Float-down fee in dollars assumed because the caller did not supply one.

since.description: Lookback window assumed for the rate-movement comparison because the caller did not supply one.

term_months.description: Loan term in months assumed because the caller did not supply one.

confidence.description: Qualitative confidence in the recommendation — 'high', 'medium', or 'low' — driven by how much data and how large the margin is.

disclosures.description: Caveats and assumptions that must accompany any answer built from this result; surface them rather than dropping them.

float_down.description: Economics of exercising a float-down to today's market rate.

available_improvement_bps.description: How far the market sits below the locked rate, in basis points (87.5 = 0.875 percentage points).

break_even_months.description: Months of savings needed to repay the float-down fee.

float_down_cost.description: Fee in dollars the lender charges to exercise the float-down.

lifetime_savings.description: Total interest in dollars saved over the full term, before the float-down fee.

monthly_savings.description: Dollars per month saved at the improved rate.

net_benefit.description: Lifetime savings less the float-down fee, in dollars — the honest headline number.

projected_rate.description: Rate in percent the borrower would move to by floating down.

worth_it.description: True when the float-down clears its cost on these assumptions.

lock.description: The borrower's existing rate lock and how much time is left on it.

days_remaining.description: Days left before the lock expires; the decision window for acting.

expired.description: True when the lock has already lapsed, in which case the float-down analysis no longer applies.

locked_rate.description: Rate in percent the borrower has locked.

market_now.description: Best deal currently available in the market, for comparison against the locked rate.

best_lender.description: Credit union publishing that best rate.

best_rate.description: Best published rate in percent available right now.

monthly_payment.description: Monthly principal-and-interest payment in dollars at that best rate.

movement.description: How the market has moved over the comparison window, from the earlier snapshot to now.

direction.description: Direction of the median move over the window: 'up', 'down', or 'flat'.

median_delta_pct.description: Change in the median APR over the window, in percentage points (0.25 = 25 basis points). Negative means rates fell.

now.description: Current market snapshot (min, median, max APR in percent, offer count, and as-of timestamp).

then.description: Market snapshot at the start of the window, for comparison against `now`. Its `count` is often much smaller because history is retention-bounded.

next_actions.description: Suggested follow-up tools that would deepen this answer; offer them as next steps, not as results.

tool.description: Name of the follow-up MCP tool to call next.

why.description: One-line reason this follow-up tool would be useful given the current result.

note.description: A caveat about the inputs or data behind this call, not an error — e.g. the supplied lock-expiration date is already in the past, so the economics assume a fresh re-lock at current market. Present only when such a caveat applies; carry it into any answer.

product_type.description: Loan or deposit category this result covers, e.g. 'mortgage', 'auto_loan', 'heloc', 'savings'.

rationale.description: Plain-English explanation of why this recommendation was reached; safe to quote to the user as the reasoning.

state.description: Two-letter US state code the result is scoped to (e.g. 'CA'). Null means the result was not filtered by state.

window.description: Lookback period used for the comparison, expressed as a short duration string such as '4w', '90d', or '180d'.
